newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria cabinet approves draft banking law.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria cabinet approves draft banking law.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim cabinet on Thursday approved a new draft banking law setting stricter regulations to bring local banks up to international standards, Economic Policy Minister Krassimir Angarski said.
"The new regulations are aimed at improving banks' licensing and setting up guarantees against bank fraud," Angarski told reporters.
Only joint stock companies with a minimum capital of five million Ecus will be eligible for a bank licence, Angarski said.
At present, the minimum capital required for domestic banking operations is set at 1.4 billion levs, and at 2.2 billion levs for local and international operations.
Companies and institutions as legal entities will no longer be able to be banks' board members. This would avoid dispersal of responsibility, said Angarski.
The draft also aims to speed up the insolvency procedure, requiring courts to rule on an insolvency within 30 days after the central bank files an insolvency procedure.
International audits of local banks will become compulsory and should be performed at least once every three years.
"According to the draft an international audit may be performed every year if there are sufficient financial resources," Angarski said.
The draft also sets qualification requirements for bankers who will be granted certificates by a central bank commission.
Under the draft people with a degree in economics, finance or law, and who have not been board members of companies declared insolvent, will be allowed to become bankers.
Banks' licences would be granted for a six-month period on the basis of capital raised, bankers' certificates granted and the bankers' tax statements for the last five years, Angarski said.

The law will go to parliament for approval. A new banking law along with the Bulgarian National Bank law is a key part of Bulgaria's agreement with the International Monetary Fund, which includes introduction of a currency board system.

So far Bulgarian courts have declared bankrupt four banks out of a total of 17 private and state owned institutions or a third of the country's banks whose insolvency has been sought by the central bank since May 1996. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188
